technical_corrections.what: Added `mkdir -p /tmp/npm-pack` to the staging step, before `npm pack --pack-destination /tmp/npm-pack`.
technical_corrections.why: MEASURED: `npm pack --pack-destination <dir>` does NOT create the destination directory — with a non-existent directory it fails `npm error enoent ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<dir>/<name>.tgz'` and exit 254. The spec's bullet assumed the pack lands in a fresh path, so the mkdir is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
technical_corrections.evidence: PROBE 1 of evidence/tui/dsh-tui-015/npm-publish/npm-probes.sh, transcript beside it: npm 11.19.0 on a throwaway fixture package -> `npm error enoent ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<dir>/probe-fixture-9.9.9.tgz'`, exit 254, no directory created. The workflow comment records the same measurement.

technical_corrections.what: Kept `npm stage approve <stage_id>` as spec'd, but added a credential preflight that fails BY NAME, plus the measured bound in the step comment.
technical_corrections.why: MEASURED, and this is a functional gap in the spec as written: `npm stage approve` CANNOT run on the trusted-publisher OIDC token. npm's own manual shipped with npm 11.19.0 (`npm-stage(1)`) states that a short-lived token issued through a trust relationship 'can only be used with `npm stage publish` and `npm publish`' and that short-lived tokens 'cannot run `npm stage` subcommands', while `npm stage approve` is listed as the subcommand that REQUIRES 2FA. The CLI confirms it: only `lib/commands/publish.js` calls the OIDC exchange (`lib/utils/oidc.js`) — `lib/commands/stage/approve.js` calls npm-registry-fetch with no OIDC path at all. So on a runner with no stored credential the approve mode would end in a bare ENEEDAUTH. The fix keeps the mode (a credential supplied in the runner environment still works), keeps the file secret-free, and turns the failure into an actionable message.
technical_corrections.evidence: PROBES 4 and 5 of evidence/tui/dsh-tui-015/npm-publish/npm-probes.sh: `grep -rln oidc lib/commands/` returns only publish.js (plus trust/circleci.js), and lib/commands/stage/approve.js in full shows the plain npmFetch POST with no OIDC exchange; man/man1/npm-stage.1 lines 19/63/76 state the trust-token restriction and the 2FA requirement for approve.

technical_corrections.what: Corrected my own first draft's credential advice: it named `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`, which npm itself does not read.
technical_corrections.why: MEASURED: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` appears NOWHERE in the whole npm 11.19.0 installation (`grep -rln NODE_AUTH_TOKEN <npm root>` → no file). It works only because `setup-node`'s `registry-url` writes an `.npmrc` interpolating it — the very input this workflow omits. npm's native mechanism is `npm_config_*` (`@npmcli/config/lib/index.js:345`, `/^npm_config_/i`), so the message now names an `.npmrc` `_authToken` entry plus `npm_config_otp`. Nothing else in the file changed.
technical_corrections.evidence: PROBE 3 of evidence/tui/dsh-tui-015/npm-publish/npm-probes.sh: `grep -rln NODE_AUTH_TOKEN <npm root>` matches 0 files across the whole npm 11.19.0 installation, while @npmcli/config/lib/index.js:346 parses `npm_config_*` — the env mechanism npm really has.

not_proven: NO LIVE WORKFLOW RUN. There is no GitHub runner, no OIDC token and no npm session here, so `npm stage publish` and `npm stage approve` were never executed against registry.npmjs.org — the rehearsal stubs npm and proves the script logic, the argument order and the guard outcomes only. The registry round-trip (stage id returned, approval applied, dist-tag moved) is UNVERIFIED from this session.
The trusted-publisher binding on npmjs.com (package @mpd-dsh/mpd -> workflow path .github/workflows/publish.yml) is the user's configuration; this session neither read nor changed it.

`actions/checkout@v7` / `actions/setup-node@v7` / `actions/upload-artifact@v4` were not executed; their availability on the runner is assumed. NOTE an inconsistency kept deliberately: the spec pinned `@v4` for upload-artifact while the repo's other two workflows (gates.yml, docker-e2e.yml) pin `@v7` — `@v4` is valid, so the spec was followed unchanged; bumping it for repo consistency is a captain's call.

The job-level env expressions (`github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.tag || github.ref_name`, `inputs.dist_tag || 'latest'`) were reasoned about, not executed: no runner evaluated them. The rehearsal fed the resolved values in directly.

The Actions YAML dialect itself: the repo gate parses with the installed harness's js-yaml, so `on:` resolves to a string here (as it does for the two existing workflows); PyYAML 1.1 does read `on:` as a boolean, which GitHub's own parser does not.
The `latest`-pointer behaviour of ascending approvals is npm's documented semantics and the spec's stated rationale; it is not measured here.
